explanation: Her book is full of lists, such as 'hateful things'. Her rival Murasaki Shikibu, author of The Tale of Genji, called her dreadfully conceited in her diary.

claims.text: Sei Shōnagon, a lady-in-waiting at the Japanese imperial court, wrote The Pillow Book around AD 1000.
Murasaki Shikibu wrote The Tale of Genji, and Ono no Komachi and Izumi Shikibu were poets; none wrote The Pillow Book.
The Pillow Book includes lists such as 'Hateful Things'.
In her diary, Murasaki Shikibu described Sei Shōnagon as 'dreadfully conceited'.

issues.note: The quoted words ('dreadfully conceited', and the list title 'Hateful Things') are one English translation's rendering; other translations phrase them differently, and the guide wants quotations verified word for word. Consider paraphrasing, or keep the quotation marks only if the source is on record. Also, as far as I recall Sei Shōnagon and Murasaki Shikibu served rival empresses at different times and probably never overlapped at court, so "her rival" is a traditional label rather than a documented rivalry.
